description: TIME-DOMAIN sample subtraction (despite living in the spectral wave's target list, it refuses .ana and takes soundfiles): output = file1 - file2, where file2 must be MONO; with a multichannel file1, -c picks which channel the subtraction hits. Verified sample-exact: self-subtraction renders digital silence (-240 dBFS); a two-file probe matched r-f exactly wherever |r-f| <= 1. OVERFLOW WRAPS, it does not clip: the 6 out-of-range samples in the probe were bit-identical to integer wraparound of the sum (the submix mix pathology). Output duration = the LONGER input (2.0 from both (2.0,1.5) and (1.5,2.0) pairs) - beyond the shorter file the remaining material continues (sign-inverted where file2 outlasts file1). Deterministic.
musical_use: The difference machine: cancel what two takes share and keep what changed. Classic uses - null-test processing chains (subtract dry from wet to hear exactly what an effect added), lift an overdub from a bounce when you still have the original bed (sample-aligned!), or create residue layers by subtracting a filtered/degraded copy from its source. Cancellation is only as good as alignment: one sample of offset turns subtraction into comb filtering (sometimes the point). Phase-sensitive by construction. Watch levels - the difference of two hot files can exceed full scale and WRAPS into harsh garbage rather than clipping; attenuate both inputs first (modify loudness / gain 0.5) when in doubt.

chan.description: Which channel of file1 the (mono) file2 is subtracted from (1-based; default channel 1). Bounded by file1's channel count, runtime-enforced: '-c3' on a stereo file1 refused verbatim 'ERROR: Channel to subtract cannot be greater than number of channels in 1st infile.' Verified live on stereo (-c2 differs from default).

examples.expected_use: Input 1 = processed render, input 2 = the dry mono source (sample-aligned) - the output is exactly what the processing added/changed.

examples.description: Subtract a bed from the right channel only.
examples.expected_use: Stereo file1, mono file2 removed from channel 2; channel 1 passes untouched.

known_issues: TIME-DOMAIN entry: .ana input refused ('ERROR: File <name> is not of correct type') - do not expect spectral subtraction (that is specnu subtract).
File 2 must be mono (banner rule); file 1 may be multichannel with -c choosing the target channel.
OVERFLOW WRAPS (verified bit-exact against integer wraparound) - the difference of two loud files comes back as full-scale garbage, not soft clipping. Stage headroom BEFORE subtracting.
Output extends to the LONGER input (verified both orders); where file2 outlasts file1 the tail is file2 negated.
Perfect cancellation requires sample alignment; any offset yields comb-filter residue instead.
